ai.literal: Than excessive anger, evil indeed is negligence in the exultation of great joy.
ai.translation: The negligence that arises from the exultation of great joy is worse than excessive anger.
ai.modern: அளவு கடந்த கோபத்தை விட, பெருமகிழ்ச்சியால் ஏற்படும் கவனக்குறைவு மிகவும் தீமையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the dangers of losing focus during moments of extreme happiness. The word 'சோர்வு' (cōrvu) here means negligence or forgetfulness of one's duties, which perfectly fits the chapter's theme of guarding against unforgetfulness. While excessive anger is widely known to be destructive, the poet argues that the distraction caused by overwhelming joy is even worse. This is because anger is an obvious enemy, whereas joy makes a person lower their guard willingly, leading to disastrous mistakes.

ai.literal: Negligence kills fame, knowledge constant poverty having killed like.
ai.translation: Negligence destroys a person's fame, just as constant poverty destroys their knowledge.
ai.modern: தொடர்ச்சியான வறுமை ஒருவனின் அறிவை அழிப்பது போல, மறதி அவனது புகழை அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a powerful parallel between the destructive effects of poverty and negligence. Just as relentless poverty ('நிச்ச நிரப்பு') wears down and destroys a person's intellect and knowledge ('அறிவினை'), negligence or forgetfulness ('பொச்சாப்பு') completely ruins their hard-earned fame ('புகழை'). The verb 'கொல்லும்' (kills) is used to emphasize the total and fatal ruin brought about by a lack of vigilance.

ai.literal: To the negligent, there is no fame; that, in the world, of any kind even to scholars, is the conclusion.
ai.translation: There is no fame for those who are negligent. That is the firm conclusion of scholars of every kind in the world.
ai.modern: மறதி உடையவர்களுக்குப் புகழ் கிடையாது. இதுவே உலகத்தில் உள்ள எவ்வகை நூல்களைக் கற்ற அறிஞர்களுக்கும் முடிவான கருத்தாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that people who are forgetful or negligent can never achieve lasting fame. The word 'பொச்சாப்பார்' refers to those who let their guard down through negligence or carelessness. The poet emphasizes that this is not merely a personal opinion, but the universal consensus ('துணிவு') of all learned people ('நூலோர்') across the world, regardless of what discipline or school of thought ('எப்பால்') they belong to. The structure firmly links the absence of fame to negligence as an undeniable, universally accepted truth.

ai.literal: Fear to those who possess, fortress is not; like that is not, negligence to those who possess, good.
ai.translation: Just as a fortress is of no use to those gripped by fear, there is no good for those who are negligent.
ai.modern: அச்சம் உடையவர்களுக்கு அரண் இருந்தாலும் பயனில்லை. அதுபோலவே, கடமையை மறக்கும் சோர்வு உடையவர்களுக்கு எந்த நன்மையும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a direct comparison between fear and negligence. A strong fortress cannot protect soldiers who are paralyzed by fear, because their internal weakness renders the external defense useless. In the exact same way, no amount of external advantage can bring success to those who are negligent. The word poccappu means a lapse in attention or forgetfulness, an internal flaw that undermines all other strengths.

ai.literal: Beforehand without-guarding he-who-erred, his fault, later disaster, grieving will-end-up.
ai.translation: He who carelessly fails to guard against faults beforehand will end up grieving when disaster strikes later.
ai.modern: முன்கூட்டியே பிழைகள் வராமல் காக்காமல் கவனக்குறைவாக இருந்தவன், பின்னர் துன்பம் வரும்போது தன் பிழையை நினைத்து வருந்துவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the dangers of negligence and lack of foresight. The word 'இழுக்கியான்' refers to someone who acts carelessly, failing to anticipate and prevent mistakes. When the inevitable consequences of this negligence manifest as disaster ('ஊறு') later on, the person is left with nothing but regret. The verse emphasizes that vigilance must be proactive, not reactive.

ai.literal: non-negligence towards-everyone always without-slipping if-attained that which-equals is-not
ai.translation: If one can unfailingly maintain non-negligence towards everyone at all times, there is nothing equal to that.
ai.modern: எவரிடத்திலும் எக்காலத்திலும் மறதி இல்லாமல் விழிப்புடன் இருக்கும் நிலை ஒருவருக்குக் கைகூடினால், அந்த நிலைக்கு இணையானது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet emphasizes the supreme value of constant vigilance or non-negligence (இழுக்காமை). It states that this quality must be maintained without slipping (வழுக்காமை) at all times and towards all people. The word 'வாய்' here takes the sense of 'to happen' or 'to be attained', fitting the conditional 'வாயின்' (if it is attained). If a person can successfully achieve this unwavering state of mindfulness, there is no other virtue or achievement that can equal it.

ai.literal: "Difficult" saying, impossible things are not, unforgetting with instrument having guarded if one does.
ai.translation: Nothing is impossible, dismissed as too difficult, if one acts carefully with an unforgetting mind.
ai.modern: மறதி இல்லாத மனமாகிய கருவியோடு ஒரு செயலைக் கவனமாகச் செய்தால், இது கடினமானது என்று சொல்லக்கூடிய முடியாத செயல் எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of unfailing attention. The phrase 'பொச்சாவாக் கருவி' refers to the instrument of an unforgetting, vigilant mind. When a person acts carefully with such a mindset ('போற்றிச் செயின்'), they avoid careless mistakes. Consequently, no task can be dismissed as too difficult ('அரிய என்று'), and nothing remains impossible ('ஆகாத இல்லை') for them to accomplish.

ai.literal: praised things having cherished doing is needed; without doing to those who neglected even in seven births there is not.
ai.translation: One must cherish and perform the deeds praised by the wise. Those who neglect and fail to do them will find no benefit in any of their seven births.
ai.modern: அறிஞர்களால் புகழப்பட்ட நற்செயல்களை மறக்காமல் போற்றிச் செய்ய வேண்டும். அவற்றைச் செய்யாமல் கைவிட்டவர்களுக்கு ஏழேழு பிறவியிலும் எந்த நன்மையும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet advises us to carefully remember and perform actions that are praised by the wise. The word 'போற்றி' (cherishing) emphasizes doing these deeds with care and without negligence. If one neglects these duties, they will not achieve any good across all seven cycles of birth.

ai.literal: Through negligence those who were ruined let them remember, they [at] their own through joy infatuation experiencing time.
ai.translation: When overcome by infatuation through their own joy, let them remember those who were ruined by negligence.
ai.modern: தாம் அடையும் பெருமகிழ்ச்சியால் செருக்குக் கொள்ளும் போது, கவனக்குறைவால் அழிந்தவர்களை நினைத்துப் பார்க்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the danger of becoming careless when experiencing great joy or success. The word 'மகிழ்ச்சி' (joy) here implies an exultation that leads to 'மைந்து' (infatuation or pride), which in turn causes negligence. To guard against this, the poet advises remembering 'கெட்டாரை' (those who were ruined) by 'இகழ்ச்சி' (negligence or forgetfulness). By recalling the downfall of others who let their guard down, one can maintain focus and avoid the same fate.

ai.literal: That which was intended attaining is easy indeed, again oneself that which was intended to remember if gets.
ai.translation: It is easy to attain what one intended, if one can only keep that intention constantly in mind.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் தான் எண்ணியதை மறக்காமல் மீண்டும் மீண்டும் நினைவில் கொள்ள முடியுமானால், அவர் எண்ணியதை அடைவது மிகவும் எளிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that achieving one's goals is remarkably easy, provided one does not lose sight of them. The word 'உள்ளியது' refers to what is thought of or intended as a goal. By repeating this word and pairing it with 'உள்ளப் பெறின்' (if one manages to remember), the poet emphasizes that constant mindfulness and freedom from negligence are the true keys to success.
